title: Singular binned information: the plug-in geometric-mean retention is biased upward at rate n^{-(d-r)/d}
statement: Under a frozen rule with iid equally weighted evaluation pairs (S_i, Z_i), positive cell probabilities, E||S||^2 < infinity and V = E[S S^T] positive definite, if I_Z = sum_b m_b m_b^T / p_b has rank r < d (so eta_D = 0), then the plug-in eta_hat_D = (det I_hat_Z / det V_hat)^(1/d) is O_p(n^{-(d-r)/d}): with U an orthonormal null basis of I_Z, U^T m_b = 0 for every cell but U^T m_hat_b = O_p(n^{-1/2}), so the null block of I_hat_Z and its Schur complement are O_p(1/n) and det I_hat_Z = O_p(n^{-(d-r)}). If moreover K >= d and E[U^T S S^T U 1{Z=b}] is positive definite for every cell, then n^{(d-r)/d} eta_hat_D converges in law to a strictly positive random variable, (det(R^T I_Z R) det(W P^{-1} W^T) / det V)^(1/d) with W = G (I - Lambda), G the (d-r) x K matrix of independent Gaussian limits of sqrt(n) U^T m_hat_b and Lambda the rank-r projection Lambda_{b'b} = (R^T m_b')^T (R^T I_Z R)^{-1} (R^T m_b) / p_b'. Consequences: at d = 1 the bias is O(1/n) (O6); at d >= 2 with r = d - 1 it is n^{-1/d}, slower than the n^{-1/2} CLT scale, the Wald half-width is measured to be of the same order as the plug-in, and coverage of the true value 0 is measured to stabilise at a law-dependent constant, not at 1 - alpha; neither is derived - the joint limit of (n^{(d-r)/d} eta_hat_D, n^{(d-r)/d} sigma_hat/sqrt(n)) is not part of this claim (audit hardening H3). The reference-law instance is K = d, where FI-RANK-CEILING forces eta_D = 0 while the sample plug-in - and the library's reported number - is positive.
assumptions: positive cell probabilities; E||S||^2 < infinity (no fourth moment is needed for the rate); V positive definite; the rule is frozen so the pairs are iid
the lower bound needs K >= d (so that K - r >= d - r) and a nondegenerate conditional second moment of the null-direction score U^T S in every cell; the upper bound needs neither
the joint law of the limits of sqrt(n) U^T m_hat_b across cells is Gaussian with independent blocks because the cross-covariances E[U^T S 1{Z=b} (U^T S 1{Z=b'})^T] vanish for b != b'
the limit law is not characterised beyond positivity; the classical setting is the dimensionality test of Seo, Kanda & Fujikoshi (1995), whose statement was not read (LITERATURE/gaps.md)

measured (O7.7 and the audit's fresh seeds): n^{1/2} eta_hat_D has mean 0.63-0.65 at n >= 1000 on the d = 2, K = 2 Hermite law against the closed-form limit mean 2/pi = 0.6366 (the limit is |G_0 + G_1|/sqrt(pi) with G_b iid N(0,1)); n^{1/3} eta_hat_D drifts 0.57 -> 0.535 at n <= 10000 on the d = 3, K = 3 law against the simulated limit mean 0.524; coverage of 0 stabilises near 0.95 and 0.80 respectively; the scaled half-width n^{(d-r)/d} z sigma_hat/sqrt(n) is measured constant (1.56, 0.97)

independently audited 6 Sep 2026 (AUDIT-RETENTION-PLUGIN-VECTOR): the Schur-complement derivation rechecked, Lambda verified idempotent of rank r on both endpoint laws, the limit law simulated from its Gaussian ingredients matches the finite-n scaled plug-in in mean and quantiles; the coverage-convergence sentence is hardened to a measured statement (H3)

proof_location.section: O7. Frozen-rule vector retention: plug-in asymptotics of the geometric-mean retention

role: the eta_D = 0 endpoint of O7: says why the Wald interval must not be used at K <= d or any rank-deficient binned information, and that the bias there is slower than n^{-1/2} in d >= 2
warning: Project-level proposition inside O7.4(b) (Schur complement of a positive semidefinite empirical Gram matrix plus the CLT for the null-direction cell moments). The classical null theory of the dimensionality test covers the same limit for Gaussian and elliptical sampling; a search gap for the fixed-partition uncentred form, not novelty. Independently audited 6 Sep 2026 (AUDITS/AUDIT-RETENTION-PLUGIN-VECTOR-001.md).
